podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaboration and Formation
podcast.body: MARRS formed in 1988 through a collaboration between members of AR Kane (Alex Ayuli, Rudy Tambala), Colorbox (Martin Young, Stephen Young), and Russell Smith, an associate of AR Kane. The name is an acronym of the members' initials.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Groundbreaking Sampling Project
podcast.body: MARRS was a collaborative studio project involving musicians, producers, and DJs associated with 4AD, and its single "Pump Up The Volume" redefined music production through extensive and diverse sampling. No one had previously deconstructed and reconstructed music in such a fashion. "No one had ever deconstructed and then reconstructed music in this fashion before."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Sampling Innovation
podcast.body: "Pump Up the Volume" was a landmark track in the use of sampling, showcasing a new art form that profoundly influenced hip hop and dance music, and is considered part of the broader Dreampop story.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Involvement in MARRS' "Pump Up the Volume"
xref.body: The rap group Eric B. and Rakim were among several artists whose contributions, including classic beats and samples, were integrated into MARRS' groundbreaking 1987 track "Pump Up the Volume." Their involvement highlights the cross-genre pollination occurring with new sampling technologies. "There were several rap groups involved including Eric B. and Rekeem."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Involvement in MARRS' "Pump Up the Volume"
xref.body: Israeli pop singer Afrahaza contributed to the studio creation of MARRS' 1987 hit "Pump Up the Volume." Her involvement was part of the eclectic mix of samples and contributions that made the song a "Frankenstein monster" of studio technology. "There was an Israeli pop singer named Afrahaza."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Sampled in MARRS' "Pump Up the Volume"
xref.body: James Brown's music was sampled and incorporated into MARRS' 1987 song "Pump Up the Volume." This demonstrates how artists from various genres, including pioneers like Brown, became source material for the emerging art of digital sampling. "There was James Brown and in there someplace is a recording of the Iranian Revolutionary Army chorus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
